infrastructure: Moldova has relatively fast internet speeds in Chișinău due to competitive fibre market, but rural coverage is sparse.
Data centre infrastructure is minimal and dependent on neighbouring countries for high-capacity routing.
The IT sector has grown but infrastructure investment remains constrained by limited capital.
talent: Moldova has produced software engineers who work largely in outsourcing for Western clients.
Technical University of Moldova and Moldova State University have limited AI research capacity.
Significant brain drain to Romania, EU countries, and Russia has depleted the talent pool.
governance: Moldova is pursuing EU accession and making governance reforms, receiving candidate status in 2022.
Data protection law is being aligned with GDPR as part of EU accession process.
Anti-corruption reforms are ongoing but progress is fragile.
investment: Moldova is one of Europe's least developed economies, with very limited AI-specific investment.
EU pre-accession funds are beginning to support digital transformation.
Diaspora remittances are a significant capital source but not directed toward AI.
economic_readiness: Europe's lowest GDP per capita nation, severely constraining domestic AI adoption capacity.
Growing IT services outsourcing sector is a foundation for future digital economy development.
EU accession process is the primary driver of economic modernisation.
